# Know what your AI wrote. Approve every change.

AI is writing more of your work. Stet makes every edit visible, attributed, and yours to accept or reject. Nothing lands without your sign-off.

Local files · Full history · Any agent

## Most tools treat AI like the final draft

The words just appear, unattributed and unreviewed. Stet treats AI like a co-author.

### Accept, reject, refine.

Edits arrive as proposals, one per paragraph. Accept the good ones. Reject the rest. Nothing lands without your call.

### Leave notes for your AI.

Write an instruction right in the doc. Your agent picks it up and the edit comes back for review. A comment thread with your co-author.

### Plain files. Any agent.

Your docs are markdown on your machine. Any AI that can read a file becomes a collaborator. No integration, no API key.

### Collaborate over GitHub.

Point Stet at a GitHub repo. When a teammate pushes a change, it shows up as a proposal to review, the same flow as an AI edit.

## Let it stand.

"Stet" is the proofreader's mark for "keep this change." Every review ends with that call. The mark is yours.

Built for people whose notes are already plain text and whose drafts start in a chat window.

Stet is an early build, free while it's in beta. I'm looking for people who write with AI every day and want a say in where this goes. Feedback lands directly with me: the Discord is fastest, email works too.
